case_content.title: Prompt #1 - Castor Manufacturer
case_content.content: Your client manufactures castors, the wheels found on the bottom of office chairs, out of a plant in West Germany and one in East Germany. Over the past two years the company’s profits have declined by 20% while revenues have been relatively flat. You have been asked to find out what is happening and suggest a course of action to reverse these trends.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Initial Approach
case_content.content:
This is a typical revenue/cost case. The candidate has already been told that revenues are flat, which should be a clue to explore the cost side of the income statement. It helps to work logically through both fixed and variable costs to see if there are any major items. Sometimes the interviewer will provide an income statement that breaks out the major cost components by percentage.

Case Type: Industry Analysis; Profitability Analysis

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Framework
case_content.content:
The candidate should use a profitability framework:

1. Revenue analysis
- Segment sales by division
- Determine whether flat overall revenue masks different divisional trends
- Examine demand trends by end market and geography

2. Cost analysis
- Break down fixed and variable costs
- Identify the largest cost components
- Compare cost changes by plant and division
- Focus on labor costs if labor is the major manufacturing cost

3. Operational and strategic implications
- Determine whether the East German plant has become structurally less competitive
- Evaluate whether demand decline in East German hospital beds is temporary or structural
- Consider production shifts, cost reduction, pricing changes, or restructuring

case_content.title: Expected Analysis - Fact Gathering
case_content.content:
Information to be divulged slowly:

The company operates in three divisions:
- 50% of sales are to hospital bed manufacturers
- 25% of sales are to mop bucket manufacturers
- 25% of sales are to chair manufacturers

The mop bucket and chair divisions are located in the West German manufacturing operation. The hospital bed division is located in the East German manufacturing operation.

Breaking out each division as a separate profit center shows:
- Revenues are up 10% for both the mop bucket and chair divisions
- Revenues are down 10% for the hospital bed division
- Profits are down 10% for both the mop bucket and chair divisions
- Profits are down 30% for the hospital bed division

Further investigation shows that labor is the major component of cost in manufacturing castors. In the past two years, wages in formerly state-regulated East Germany have skyrocketed. This is driving most of the increased costs.

Similarly, demand for hospital beds, and thus castors, in East Germany has declined as the region has become more efficient at managing its health care system.

case_content.title: Data / Calculations
case_content.content:
Overall company performance:
- Profits have declined by 20% over the past two years
- Revenues have been relatively flat

Sales mix by division:
- Hospital bed manufacturers: 50% of sales
- Mop bucket manufacturers: 25% of sales
- Chair manufacturers: 25% of sales

Manufacturing locations:
- West German plant: mop bucket and chair divisions
- East German plant: hospital bed division

Revenue trends by division:
- Mop bucket division: +10%
- Chair division: +10%
- Hospital bed division: -10%

Profit trends by division:
- Mop bucket division: -10%
- Chair division: -10%
- Hospital bed division: -30%

Cost and demand drivers:
- Labor is the major component of castor manufacturing cost
- East German wages have skyrocketed over the past two years
- Demand for hospital beds in East Germany has declined as the health care system has become more efficient

case_content.title: Key Findings
case_content.content:
The company’s flat overall revenue masks very different divisional trends. Mop bucket and chair revenues are growing, while hospital bed revenues are declining. Because hospital bed manufacturers account for 50% of sales, the hospital bed division has a large impact on total company performance.

The biggest profit decline is in the hospital bed division, where profits are down 30%. This division is located in East Germany, where wages have risen sharply after the end of state regulation. Since labor is the major manufacturing cost, wage inflation has significantly increased costs.

At the same time, demand for hospital beds in East Germany has declined as the health care system has become more efficient. The hospital bed division is therefore facing both lower demand and higher labor costs.

The profit decline is primarily driven by the East German hospital bed castor business, while the West German mop bucket and chair divisions are performing better on revenue but still experiencing profit pressure.

case_content.title: Final Recommendation
case_content.content: Based on your analysis, what recommendation would you give the client?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Final Recommendation
case_content.content:
A strong candidate should conclude that the company’s profit decline is driven mainly by the hospital bed division in East Germany. This division is suffering from rising labor costs due to sharply increasing East German wages and declining demand for hospital beds as the health care system becomes more efficient.

The client should consider shifting production out of the high-cost East German operation if feasible, improving labor productivity, automating parts of production, renegotiating prices with hospital bed customers, reducing capacity tied to the declining hospital bed segment, or reallocating resources toward the growing mop bucket and chair divisions.

The candidate should recognize that the issue is both cost-driven and revenue-driven within the hospital bed division, not simply a company-wide revenue problem.
